metadata.not_the_legal_artefact: This pack is DEMO SCAFFOLDING. The real pack is rulepack/lmpc-2011.json, written by task T-1.3 against rulepack/schema/rulepack.schema.json. Do not cite this file, do not promote it, do not copy its clause letters anywhere. See README.md in this directory.
metadata.scope_note: Rule 6(1) universal declarations only. Applicability gates (Rule 3 exemptions, small-quantity carve-outs) are NOT modelled — this pack assumes the Rules apply. That assumption is stated on screen.

provenance.note: No Legal Metrology officer has reviewed any entry in this file. Sub-clause letters are unverified and contested — see clause.alternate_readings on each declaration. Every finding is therefore capped at 'advisory'. Nothing here may be presented as a determination of law.

spatial_association.note: Stage B's geometry. Method parameters, not statutory values — nothing here is law, and none of it may be read as one. Distances are expressed in multiples of the ANCHOR'S OWN text height, so they scale with camera distance instead of being pixel counts tied to one phone. They live in the pack so tuning against the gold set is a data change (P6). HONESTY LIMIT: these defaults were sized from typography (a text row's pitch is a little over its glyph height; a two-column panel puts its values within a few glyph heights of the label) and then checked against the D-3 corpus, which is two captures of one packet. They are NOT corpus-derived numbers and must not be quoted as tuned until the corpus has variety (P8).

evidence_thresholds.note: Method parameters, not statutory values. Below either threshold the app reports INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of a verdict, rather than letting a bad capture read as a clean label (P3, P9). They live here so field tuning is a data change.

quantity_loose.description: A number with whatever word follows it. Used ONLY after an anchor has already identified the line as the quantity declaration, so that '250' with no unit is still recovered — and can then fail the standard-unit check rather than being reported as simply absent.

amount_loose.description: A bare amount. Used ONLY after a price anchor, so 'MRP 45.00' printed without a currency symbol is still recovered.

quantity_with_unit.description: A number immediately followed by a unit of mass, volume or count.

price_amount.description: A currency marker followed by an amount, or an amount followed by a currency word.

month_year.description: A month and a year: a named month, or numeric MM/YYYY and MM-YY. A dot separator requires a four-digit year, so a price such as '5.00' cannot be read as a date.

contact_point.description: An email address, or an Indian phone number of 10 or 11 digits with optional grouping, or a 1800 toll-free number.

address_like.description: A 6-digit Indian PIN code, or an address keyword. Weak by design — this field is the least reliably extracted of the six.

lexicons.note: Anchor terms are matched case-insensitively against normalised OCR lines, with a word boundary required only on the sides where the anchor itself ends in a letter or digit. Stage A takes the value from the anchor's own line. Stage B (since A-4) looks for it where it is printed — to the right of the anchor on the same row, or below it in the same column — and no longer by position in the OCR line list. See metadata.spatial_association for the bounds and scan/associate.ts for how they are used.

fields.label: Manufacturer / packer / importer name and address
fields.extraction_note: Free-text field. Recovered by anchor, then by the lines that follow it. Genuinely hard; expect misses.

fields.label: Common or generic name of the commodity
fields.extraction_note: Often the largest text on the panel with no anchor at all. Anchored recovery only; unanchored recovery is out of demo scope.

fields.label: Net quantity
fields.extraction_note: Anchored recovery only. This field claimed 'shape is distinctive enough to recover without an anchor' until the D-3 field trial falsified it: on record 002 shape-only recovery returned '15.1g', read out of the FSSAI food-category code in 'PROPRIETARY FOOD--NAMKEEN(15.1)'. A number with a mass unit is not distinctive on a food label - a nutrition panel is full of them (0.3g, 33.4g, 08g), and nothing in the line alone separates the declaration from the table. Turning this off means a packet whose 'Net Qty' anchor is missed now reports the declaration as not found, which is an advisory saying 'rescan the panel' - honest about what was read, where '15.1g' was a confident falsehood about what the label says (P3, P4). Recovering the real value from an anchor several lines away needs spatial association, which A-4 (T-2.3) delivered on 2026-09-10: on record 002 the true '84.9g' is now reached from the 'NET QTY:' anchor because it is printed 2.6 anchor-heights to its right, nineteen entries away in the OCR list. Unanchored recovery stays OFF — that fix and this one are independent, and the shape is still not distinctive on a nutrition panel.

fields.label: Retail sale price (MRP), inclusive of all taxes
fields.extraction_note: Shape is distinctive enough to recover without an anchor.

fields.label: Month and year of manufacture, packing or import
fields.extraction_note: Best-before / use-by dates are deliberately NOT accepted here — that is an FSSAI declaration, not this one. See the open question in docs/PROGRESS.md.

fields.label: Consumer care contact
fields.extraction_note: Shape is distinctive enough to recover without an anchor.

clause.note: The (a) position for manufacturer/packer/importer particulars is the least contested of the six, but is still unverified.

declarations.title: Manufacturer / packer / importer particulars not found
declarations.requirement: Every package must carry the name and complete address of the manufacturer, or of the packer or importer where the manufacturer is not the packer.
declarations.remedy: Check the rear or side panel for a 'Manufactured by' / 'Marketed by' block and rescan that panel.

declarations.title: Common or generic name of the commodity not found
declarations.requirement: Every package must state the common or generic name of the commodity contained in it.
declarations.remedy: The brand name is not the commodity name. Look for a descriptive term such as 'biscuits' or 'refined sunflower oil'.

declarations.title: Net quantity not found
declarations.requirement: Every package must declare the net quantity, in terms of the standard unit of weight, measure or number.
declarations.remedy: Rescan the panel that carries the quantity declaration.

clause.note: The requirement that the quantity be expressed in a standard unit is read into the same sub-clause. Unverified.

declarations.title: Net quantity carries no standard unit
declarations.requirement: The net quantity must be expressed in the standard unit of weight, measure or number — not as a bare figure.
declarations.remedy: Confirm visually whether a unit is printed and simply missed by the scan.

alternate_readings.note: v1 of this project's own spec placed the retail sale price at (1)(f). Not resolved.

clause.note: CONTESTED. The common reading places retail sale price at 6(1)(e); this project's v1 spec placed it at 6(1)(f). Both are shown until a Legal Metrology officer confirms one.

declarations.title: Retail sale price (MRP) not found
declarations.requirement: Every package must declare the retail sale price as 'Maximum retail price Rs ... inclusive of all taxes'.
declarations.remedy: Rescan the panel carrying the price. A price sticker applied over the printed panel is itself worth recording.

check.requires_anchored_field_note: This check may only FAIL when the price was located by an anchor (stage A or B). Recovered by shape alone (stage C) the check is skipped, not failed. D-3 record 002: the packet does carry the wording, OCR returned 'MIRP RS. 20/- (NCL. OF 42L TAYES)', the phrase match failed, and a compliant declaration was flagged. Saying 'the prescribed wording is absent' is a claim about what is printed; a scan that could not even read the letters M-R-P, and found the price only because a rupee sign happened to survive, has no warrant to make it (P3, P9). Where the anchor WAS read the label was legible and the finding stands. This is not OCR-noise tolerance in the phrase list - no fuzzy or edit-distance matching is done anywhere in the demo, and adding literal variants of one packet's garble would overfit the pack to it. Character-confusion repair is T-2.1, measured against the gold set.

alternate_readings.note: Follows whichever letter the price declaration takes.

clause.note: CONTESTED, as above. The prescribed form of the price declaration includes the words 'inclusive of all taxes'.

declarations.title: Price declaration does not say 'inclusive of all taxes'
declarations.requirement: The retail sale price must be declared in the prescribed form, which includes the words 'inclusive of all taxes'.
declarations.remedy: Confirm visually. This phrase is frequently printed in very small type and is a common OCR miss.

alternate_readings.note: v1 of this project's own spec placed the date at (1)(g). Not resolved.

clause.note: CONTESTED. The common reading places the date at 6(1)(d); this project's v1 spec placed it at 6(1)(g).

declarations.title: Month and year of manufacture / packing not found
declarations.requirement: Every package must declare the month and year in which the commodity was manufactured, packed or imported.
declarations.remedy: A 'best before' date is not this declaration. Look specifically for a manufacture or packing date.

alternate_readings.note: Position depends on how the price and date sub-clauses resolve.

clause.note: CONTESTED. This letter shifts depending on how the price and date sub-clauses resolve.

declarations.title: Consumer care contact not found
declarations.requirement: Every package must carry consumer care details — the name, address, telephone number or email of the person to be contacted about consumer complaints.
declarations.remedy: Look for a helpline, toll-free number or email address, usually near the manufacturer block.
